outcomes: A GitLab CI pipeline adds observe with one include: component: gitlab.com/putnami/observe/observe@1 line after its tests and reads the change summary in its log, with no install line to copy

On gitlab.com, with its organization id as an input, the same job exchanges its ID token for a short-lived upload token, uploads the change evidence document and posts on the merge request, with no Putnami secret in the project
A release of the component publishes a semantic version to the GitLab CI/CD catalog, so a pipeline that names @1 runs the newest compatible component
nonGoals: Publishing on the merge request without a project access token: the GitLab job token cannot write notes, so --publish reads PUTNAMI_GITLAB_TOKEN, a masked CI/CD variable the project sets
The ID token exchange on a self-managed GitLab: Putnami Cloud verifies the ID tokens of gitlab.com only, so such a job sets PUTNAMI_CLOUD_TOKEN as a masked CI/CD variable
Pushing to gitlab.com from this repository's CI: an owner runs the release script against a clone of the catalog project with their own credentials
Relaying a fork's evidence: a GitLab merge request from a fork runs in the fork's project, whose ID token names the fork

text: The component templates/observe.yml declares one job, observe, that runs one bash script.

It installs the Putnami CLI with https://putnami.dev/install.sh, puts ~/.putnami/bin on the PATH, and installs @putnami/observe in the user scope, all from the channel input, stable when empty, which reads latest as putnami upgrade reads it;
it installs @putnami/cloud too only when the job uploads.

requirements.text: A channel input that is a version, or outside the channel alphabet of putnami init (a lowercase letter or a digit, then lowercase letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-', 64 characters at most), fails the job before any install: the release lines do not share one version.

text: The stage, needs and image inputs set the job's stage, needs and image: test, the job named test with its artifacts as an optional need, so a pipeline without it is still created, and an image with Bash, curl, tar, sha256sum and Git by default.

The job runs putnami observe with --evidence observe-evidence.json in the project directory, runs when a test job failed too, keeps that document as an artifact whatever the outcome, and sets no clone depth.
Each input reaches the script as a PUTNAMI_OBSERVE_* job variable, never interpolated into the script text, so an input value cannot change a command.
Each of the junit, coverage, sbom, base-sbom and base inputs that is not empty becomes the flag of the same name with its value; an empty input passes no flag.
The job's id_tokens declares one ID token, PUTNAMI_ID_TOKEN, whose only aud is the auth server's base URL with no trailing slash, https://auth.putnami.cloud.
With the organization input set, the job sets PUTNAMI_ORGANIZATION to it and runs putnami observe with --upload, so @putnami/cloud exchanges PUTNAMI_ID_TOKEN for an upload token.
With PUTNAMI_CLOUD_TOKEN set as a CI/CD variable, the job uploads with it, and it wins over the exchange.
With neither it nor the organization input, the job prints the summary and writes the evidence document, and uploads nothing.
The publish input, a boolean true by default, adds --publish when the job uploads; false keeps the upload without the commit status and the note.
The installer and the extension installs see none of PUTNAMI_ID_TOKEN, PUTNAMI_CLOUD_TOKEN, PUTNAMI_GITLAB_TOKEN and the job token; putnami observe keeps the job token for Git only.
PUTNAMI_ID_TOKEN reaches putnami observe only when it exchanges it: with the organization input set and no PUTNAMI_CLOUD_TOKEN.
PUTNAMI_GITLAB_TOKEN reaches putnami observe only when the job uploads and publishes.

release.sh <X.Y.Z> <clone> replaces the root of a clone of the catalog project with templates/observe.yml, the component's README.md, its project pipeline as .gitlab-ci.yml and LICENSE.md, in one commit tagged X.Y.Z, pushed with the checked-out branch in one atomic push.
A version that is not X.Y.Z, or a tag the clone's origin already holds, stops before any write.

requirements.text: The project pipeline creates the release with the release keyword in a pipeline for an X.Y.Z tag only, which publishes that version to the GitLab CI/CD catalog, and runs no other job.
